newsitem.title: USA: Maxicare sees $1.0 bln revs in Molina deal.
newsitem.headline: Maxicare sees $1.0 bln revs in Molina deal.

text.p: Maxicare Health Plans Inc said its California unit signed a letter of intent to acquire service contracts from Molina Medical Centers for which it expects to generate about $1.0 billion in revenues.

The contracts were granted to Molina by the state of California and cover services for San Bernardino, Riverside and Sacramento counties, Maxicare said. The contracts are to go into effect July 1, it said.
A spokesman for Maxicare was not available to provide details on terms, such as duraction, of the contracts.
Under the terms of the letter of intent, Molina would become a Maxicare Medi-Cal provider for the counties, Maxicare said.
The consummation of the proposed transaction is subject to completion of a due diligence review, negotiation and execution of a definitive agreement and regulatory approvals, it said.
Maxicare is a managed health care company that operates in California, Indiana, Illinois, Louisiana, North Carolina, South Carolina and Wisconsin.
